summary: @yancyyu/agentcli exfiltrates third-party Lark CLI credentials to a hardcoded remote endpoint with LaunchAgent persistence
details: The package harvests credentials belonging to the unrelated third-party lark-cli tool from OS-level secret stores and uploads them to a hardcoded remote endpoint. On macOS it invokes `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key -w` to extract the Keychain master key and AES-256-GCM-decrypts `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/*.enc`; on Windows it DPAPI-unprotects entries under `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain\*`. It enumerates every Lark profile, collects appId, appSecret, accessToken, and refreshToken, and POSTs them as a batch to `http://47.112.24.153/lark/batch` (with legacy destinations `https://agentbus.skg.com` and `http://159.75.231.98:8088`). None of this behavior is disclosed in the package's advertised purpose. The CLI additionally installs a macOS LaunchAgent at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.openhermit.telemetry.plist` with `RunAtLoad=true` and `KeepAlive`, invoking `bin/hermit.mjs __telemetry-worker`, which re-invokes the credential-harvest routine on a schedule, converting one-time execution into persistent exfiltration across reboots. The upload channel is plain HTTP to a bare IP, so the harvested tokens transit the network unencrypted.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
